key_insight: Separating fast acoustics from slow mean motion enables long-time, fully resolved particle simulations while retaining two-way fluid–structure coupling.
engineering_relevance: The framework could improve acoustofluidic particle-manipulation predictions by resolving density-dependent motion, streaming, and particle rotation.
method: Split dynamics into time-harmonic first-order acoustics and time-averaged second-order flow.
Represent rigid particles using immersed-boundary/Brinkman volume penalization.
Derive order-consistent particle velocities and equations of motion, including Stokes drift.
evidence_signal: Two-dimensional circular-particle simulations show substantial streaming differences between fixed and freely moving particles, while elliptical-particle simulations demonstrate coupled translation and rotation.
watch_item: Moving-interface consistency is a key implementation concern; the abstract reports no quantitative error or speedup benchmarks.
paper_title: Fully resolved particle dynamics over long time scales in acoustofluidic flows: Theory and numerical simulations
